mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate earnings expectations, thus driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 2% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% MoM signals a strengthening housing market, which can boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% MoM signals increased consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.
